question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that $49,{h}^{2},$ and ${k}^{2}$ are perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{49{h}^{2}{k}^{2}} & =\sqrt{{7}^{2}\cdot {h}^{2}\cdot {k}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{7\cdot 7\cdot h\cdot h\cdot k\cdot k} \\  & =\sqrt{7\cdot h\cdot k\cdot 7\cdot h\cdot k} \\  & =\sqrt{(7hk)\cdot (7hk)} \\  & =\sqrt{(7hk)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(7hk)^{2}} & =|7hk| \\  & =|7|\cdot |hk| \\  & =7|hk|\end{aligned}
$$
